topics.title: Make your first vinyl
topics.summary: Choose an image, generate shape files, inspect one, import it, and save the result in the game.
steps: Open Create and choose the image you want to reproduce. A clean PNG with a transparent background is the easiest starting point.
Keep the preset KFPS chooses automatically. Leave the advanced options off; 2x Mode is the only extra option most people should try.
Choose a shape limit. This is the most shapes KFPS may use, and it must fit the template you will open in the game.
Select Generate Vinyl. Keep KFPS open until the status says finalization is complete.
Open Outputs, choose Generated finals, and click the finished vinyl you want to use.
Prepare the running game. For FH6, open your saved, reopened, and ungrouped circle template in Vinyl Group Editor.
Choose the correct game and exact template layer count, then select Online Import to Game.
Wait for the transfer to finish. Save the vinyl in the game, leave the editor, and reopen it before judging the final result.

sections.heading: What KFPS makes
sections.body: KFPS turns a normal image into a list of Forza shapes. That list is stored in a JSON file. The generator makes the first version; the manual editor is available when you want to move, recolor, group, or replace individual shapes.

sections.heading: What online means here
sections.body: Online import and export do not upload your artwork. Online means KFPS talks to a game that is running on this computer through live memory. Offline means KFPS works with supported local game save files instead.

sections.heading: The normal path
sections.body: For most work, use Create -> Outputs -> Online Import to Game. Use the manual editor only when the generated result needs changes that require your judgment.

pitfalls: Do not run KFPS from GitHub's main/source ZIP. Use an official release folder.
Do not import a raw checkpoint when a finished JSON is available in the finals folder.
Do not guess the game template layer count. Enter the number shown by the open template.
Do not switch game menus while an online transfer is locating or writing layers.

topics.title: Choose a good source image
topics.summary: A clean, readable source saves time and prevents shapes from being wasted on a background or compression noise.
steps: Choose the source on Create or in Image Tools.
Check that the subject fills the image and is not tiny inside a large empty border.
Use transparency for cutout art when possible. A checkerboard visible in an image viewer is a useful sign, but still check for a hidden solid background.
Read the source check. Fix red warnings before a long run; review yellow warnings before deciding to continue.
Use Preview Detail Map to see where KFPS detects edges and small features.

sections.heading: Good sources
sections.body: Logos, illustrations, and characters work best when their edges are clear and important details are large enough to see. A larger file is not automatically better if it is blurry or heavily compressed.

sections.heading: Transparent versus solid backgrounds
sections.body: Transparent PNGs are best for stickers and cutout art. If the background is part of the design, keep it. If it is not, remove it before generation so the shape budget is spent on the subject.

pitfalls: Upscaling cannot restore detail that is completely missing from the source.
Very thin lines may still need manual editor cleanup after generation.
A hidden nearly solid background can consume hundreds of shapes.

topics.title: Presets and generation options
topics.summary: Let KFPS choose a preset first, then change only what solves a visible problem.
steps: Choose a source image and let KFPS select a preset.
Use Flat Colors for logos, text, icons, and art with clear color regions.
Use Shaded Art for illustrations or subjects with normal light and shadow.
Use Gradients for smooth color changes where banding would be obvious.
Leave Detail Heatmap, Luma Prep, and Edge Repair off unless you are testing a specific problem.
Try 2x Mode when the normal run needs better shape choices and you can accept a longer run.

sections.heading: Automatic choices
sections.body: KFPS inspects the selected image and chooses suitable defaults. The checkboxes let advanced users force parts of that preparation, but forcing every option does not produce a better image.

sections.heading: 2x Mode
sections.body: 2x Mode spends roughly twice the search work looking for useful shape matches. It may improve edges, small details, or shading, but it also takes longer. It does not double the final shape count.

sections.heading: Manual overrides
sections.body: Settings can reveal resolution, random sample, mutated sample, and seed fields. These are testing controls. Presets already fill normal values, so leave Manual generator overrides off unless you understand the tradeoff you are measuring.

pitfalls: Turning on every option can reduce quality or make a run much slower.
Changing several advanced values at once makes comparisons difficult.
The same seed helps repeat a search, but different software or source changes can still change the result.

topics.title: Shape limit and finished checkpoints
topics.summary: Set one maximum shape budget and save usable finished versions at smaller counts along the way.
steps: Set Template layers to the largest shape count you want this run to reach.
Keep that number at or below the number of editable layers in your game template.
List the counts you want saved in Finalize checkpoints, separated by commas.
Let generation and finalization finish before closing KFPS.
In Outputs, compare the finished versions and choose the lowest count that keeps the detail you need.

sections.heading: Why save several counts
sections.body: A 1500-shape result may look almost the same as a 2000-shape result and be easier to edit or import. Finished checkpoints let you compare without rerunning the entire search.

sections.heading: Finished versus raw
sections.body: Raw checkpoints are recovery data from the search. Finished JSONs are checked, limited to the requested budget, previewed, and prepared for normal import. Use the finals folder unless you are recovering a damaged run.

sections.heading: Where the files go
sections.body: Each job under imgs/generated has separate finals, checkpoints, previews, and reports folders. Outputs normally shows the finished JSONs for you.

pitfalls: More shapes do not guarantee a visibly better result.
A JSON cannot fit into an online template with fewer editable layers.
Closing during finalization can leave raw checkpoints without finished JSONs.

topics.title: Read generation progress
topics.summary: Use the preview and live log to tell normal progress from a stopped or failed run.
steps: After selecting Generate Vinyl, watch the status and live output preview.
Expect the preview to update in steps rather than after every shape.
Wait for finalization after the search reaches its target. This is when finished JSONs and their previews are written.
Use Stop Safely when you want completed work saved before the run ends.
Use Stop Now only when safe stopping does not respond. Completed checkpoints are kept, but the active step is lost.

sections.heading: Normal pauses
sections.body: Some steps take longer because KFPS is testing many candidates, writing a checkpoint, or building previews. A quiet preview alone does not mean the process has failed; check the status and log.

sections.heading: After a failure
sections.body: Keep the job folder and its reports. A later run can be compared with the last completed checkpoint, and the log usually identifies whether the generator, finalizer, or file write failed.

pitfalls: Do not close the console or KFPS while finalization is still running.
Do not assume the highest checkpoint is finished until its JSON and preview appear in finals/previews.
Repeated force stops can leave incomplete temporary files.

topics.title: Use the Outputs browser
topics.summary: Choose a source, search by vinyl name, inspect thumbnails, and select the exact JSON you want.
steps: Open Outputs and choose an Output source.
Use Generated finals for generator results, Editor exports for manual-editor work, and Game exports for JSON read from a running game.
Use Library for vinyls found by an offline save scan.
Type part of a vinyl name in Search to filter only the current source. Empty the box to show everything again.
Click a thumbnail once to select it. Double-click it to open a larger preview and file details.
Check the displayed shape count before importing.

sections.heading: Manual JSON files
sections.body: Add JSON lets you choose a compatible file outside the normal folders. When a supported Forza Designer 6 shapes file is chosen, KFPS detects and converts it in the background without changing the original file.

sections.heading: Thumbnails
sections.body: KFPS caches previews so later starts are faster. A missing preview does not make a valid JSON unusable; select or refresh the source and allow the thumbnail index to finish.

sections.heading: Library items
sections.body: Library items came from local game save files. They are already in that game's saved library, so the live online-import button is intentionally unavailable for that source.

pitfalls: Output search only filters the source currently selected.
Two vinyls can have similar names. Check the preview, folder, and shape count.
Raw generator checkpoints are hidden from normal browsing because finished files are safer.

topics.title: Make the FH6 import template
topics.summary: Create one flat group of 3000 white circles, save and reopen it once, then ungroup it before every online import.
steps: Start FH6 and open Vinyl Group Editor. Do not use the car livery screen or the screen that only applies a saved vinyl.
Create or load a vinyl group made from 3000 simple plain white circle layers. The circles are placeholders; their size and position do not matter.
Make sure all 3000 circles are individual layers. Do not leave smaller groups nested inside the template.
Save this circle group in FH6 once.
Leave the group editor, reopen the saved circle group, and choose Ungroup so individual circle layers are visible and editable.
Stay on that editor screen. In KFPS Outputs, choose FH6 and enter 3000 for Template layers.
Reuse this same saved template for later imports: reopen it, ungroup it, and keep the exact count in KFPS.

sections.heading: Why KFPS needs it
sections.body: Online import replaces layer slots that already exist in the running game. It cannot create thousands of new live layers from an empty FH6 group, so the circles provide safe editable slots for the imported design.

sections.heading: Why save and reopen once
sections.body: FH6 does not always expose a newly created group in the same stable state as a saved group. Saving, leaving, and reopening gives the locator a predictable live layer table.

sections.heading: How to know it is ready
sections.body: You are inside Vinyl Group Editor, the template itself is open, individual circles can be selected, no nested group is selected as one object, and KFPS shows the same layer count as FH6.

sections.heading: Smaller templates
sections.body: A smaller flat template can work when its exact count is entered, but it can only accept a JSON with that many shapes or fewer. The 3000-circle template is recommended because it covers the full supported budget.

pitfalls: A grouped template looks like one object and cannot be used as 3000 editable slots.
Do not leave duplicate template groups stacked above the group you intend to edit.
Do not enter the JSON shape count when KFPS asks for the template count unless those numbers are actually equal.
Do not switch FH6 menus after starting an online import.

topics.title: Online import into FH6
topics.summary: Open the correct FH6 template, select a finished JSON, enter the exact count, and let KFPS locate and replace the live layers.
steps: Start FH6 and open your saved circle template in Vinyl Group Editor.
Ungroup the template and confirm individual layers can be selected.
Open Outputs in KFPS, choose FH6, and enter the template's exact layer count, normally 3000.
Choose Generated finals, Editor exports, or Game exports, then select the JSON you want.
Leave Clear Extra Template Layers on for normal use.
Select Online Import to Game and do not change screens in FH6 while KFPS locates and writes the layers.
When the transfer reports success, save the vinyl in FH6, leave the editor, and reopen it to check the final result.

sections.heading: Location is automatic
sections.body: KFPS searches the running FH6 process for the open template when you import. You do not need a separate locate button. Restart the import after reopening the template if FH6 was restarted or the editor screen changed.

sections.heading: Clear extra layers
sections.body: If the JSON uses fewer shapes than the template, this option hides the unused placeholder circles. Leave it enabled unless you are doing a controlled transfer test.

sections.heading: Permission
sections.body: KFPS and FH6 must be running on the same Windows computer. If Windows blocks live memory access, run KFPS with the same or higher permission level as the game.

pitfalls: Applying a vinyl to a car is not the same as editing a vinyl group.
A stale or wrong layer count can make location fail or find the wrong group.
Do not touch FH6 until KFPS says the transfer is complete.
Save and reopen before deciding that a live thumbnail or shape resource is wrong.

topics.title: Online and offline transfer
topics.summary: Online works with a running game; offline works with supported local save files.
steps: For online export, open the vinyl group in the running ga…1473 tokens truncated….
Use a source overlay as a visual reference and adjust its opacity when it hides the vinyl.
Turn snapping off for small freehand corrections.

sections.heading: Guides do not export
sections.body: The grid, guides, selection outlines, and source overlay are editor aids. They are not Forza shapes and are not written into the exported JSON.

sections.heading: Zoom and performance
sections.body: The editor reuses cached shape geometry. Extremely dense art can still be slower when every tiny shape is visible, so hide unused panels or layers while making detailed changes.

pitfalls: Snapping that is useful for a logo may fight small organic adjustments.
An opaque source overlay can make correct shapes look missing.
Judge line thickness in the exported preview, not from the selection outline.

topics.title: Open and save editor projects
topics.summary: Use the manual editor for changes that need human judgment, then keep the project and export JSON as separate files.
steps: Open Editor in KFPS.
Choose New Project for a blank canvas, or select a saved project and choose Open Project.
Import a JSON or build with shapes inside the editor.
Save a project when you want to keep editable state, guides, overlays, and groups.
Export a JSON when the design is ready to import into a game.

sections.heading: Project versus JSON
sections.body: A project is the editor's working document. A JSON is the portable shape list used by Outputs and the game transfer tools. Keep the project if you may edit the design again.

sections.heading: Why use the editor
sections.body: The generator is good at broad visual matching. The editor is better for exact text, logos, eyes, outlines, alignment, deliberate grouping, and small corrections.

pitfalls: Closing a browser editor window before saving can lose unsaved changes.
Exporting a JSON does not automatically replace the saved editor project.
Very large projects may take a moment to load even with cached shape rendering.

topics.title: Select, arrange, and group shapes
topics.summary: Understand layer order, multi-selection, groups, and the difference between moving one shape and moving a set.
steps: Select a shape on the canvas or in the layer list.
Use multi-selection when several shapes must move, scale, or rotate together.
Group shapes that form one logical feature, such as a letter, eye, or badge.
Use layer order to place foreground shapes above background shapes.
Save the project before a large regrouping or reordering change.

sections.heading: Layer order
sections.body: Shapes are drawn in order. Moving a layer forward can reveal it; moving it backward can hide it behind another shape.

sections.heading: Groups
sections.body: A group lets related shapes transform together without permanently flattening their individual editor data. Game exports may represent grouping differently, so inspect the exported preview.

sections.heading: Selection outline
sections.body: The highlight stays thin on screen as you zoom. It shows the editor selection and is not part of the exported vinyl.

pitfalls: Moving a parent group and one of its selected children together can apply a transform twice in poorly formed imports.
A shape hidden behind another layer is not necessarily deleted.
Keep groups simple when the final target has limited grouping behavior.

topics.title: Use snapping, guides, and overlays
topics.summary: Align shapes precisely without making reference images or guides part of the exported vinyl.
steps: Zoom to the area you want to adjust.
Enable the grid or guide type that matches the alignment you need.
Turn snapping on when shapes should lock to those guides.
Use a source overlay as a visual reference and adjust its opacity when it hides the vinyl.
Turn snapping off for small freehand corrections.

sections.heading: Guides do not export
sections.body: The grid, guides, selection outlines, and source overlay are editor aids. They are not Forza shapes and are not written into the exported JSON.

sections.heading: Zoom and performance
sections.body: The editor reuses cached shape geometry. Extremely dense art can still be slower when every tiny shape is visible, so hide unused panels or layers while making detailed changes.

pitfalls: Snapping that is useful for a logo may fight small organic adjustments.
An opaque source overlay can make correct shapes look missing.
Judge line thickness in the exported preview, not from the selection outline.

topics.title: Export from the manual editor
topics.summary: Save editable work as a project, then export a game-ready JSON for Outputs.
steps: Save the editor project so you can return to the exact working state.
Check the shape count against the game template you plan to use.
Export the design as JSON from the editor.
Return to KFPS Outputs and choose Editor exports.
Select the exported JSON, inspect its thumbnail and shape count, then import it normally.

sections.heading: Two files, two jobs
sections.body: The project keeps editor-only information. The exported JSON is the transfer file. Saving one does not replace the other.

sections.heading: Before import
sections.body: Check that the export contains only intended shapes, stays within the target layer budget, and has the expected canvas placement.

pitfalls: Do not delete the project just because the JSON exported successfully.
A JSON over the template budget must be reduced before online import.
Refresh Editor exports if a new file does not appear immediately.

topics.title: Build pixel art
topics.summary: Use a fixed grid and repeated square shapes for deliberate pixel-style designs.
steps: Choose a grid size that fits the target shape budget.
Use a clear source with hard pixel edges and no smoothing.
Create or paint the grid cells with a small controlled palette.
Check the total shape count before exporting.
Inspect the exported preview at normal size as well as zoomed in.

sections.heading: Budget
sections.body: One filled cell usually costs one shape. A 40 by 40 fully filled grid can already require 1600 shapes before extra outlines or corrections.

sections.heading: Clean edges
sections.body: Avoid source scaling that blurs pixels. Hard edges and a limited palette are easier to reproduce consistently.

pitfalls: A grid larger than the layer budget cannot be fully represented.
Anti-aliased source pixels can create unwanted extra colors.
Tiny gaps may become more visible after the game rescales the vinyl.

topics.title: Prepare images before generation
topics.summary: Remove unwanted backgrounds, enlarge genuinely small sources, or convert oversized files before a long run.
steps: Open Tools.
Use Remove background when the subject should be transparent but the source has a solid or messy background.
Use Upscale small sources only when important details are too small for the generator to read.
Use Resize or compress when a file is unnecessarily huge or in an awkward format.
Save the prepared result as a clear PNG or another supported format, then run Source image check again.

sections.heading: External websites
sections.body: The Tools buttons open third-party websites in your browser. KFPS does not upload the image itself. Read each site's terms and privacy information before submitting private artwork.

sections.heading: Keep the original
sections.body: Prepare a copy so you can compare results or return to the untouched source later.

pitfalls: Background removal can erase thin lines or pale details; inspect the edges closely.
Upscaling a blurry image can make it larger without making it more accurate.
Heavy compression adds blocks and halos that waste shapes.

topics.title: Create a useful local report
topics.summary: Describe a bug or suggestion, review optional private context, and save a text report locally.
steps: Open Settings and choose Create Report, or open Reports directly.
Choose Bug or Suggestion and enter a short title.
Write what you clicked, what happened, what you expected, and the last step that worked.
Choose whether to include the app version, visible log, or local paths.
Preview the report and remove anything private you do not want to share.
Save the report. KFPS does not send it automatically.

sections.heading: Privacy
sections.body: Runtime logs can contain filenames. Local paths can contain your Windows username. Those options are off or clearly labeled so you can decide what to include.

sections.heading: Useful evidence
sections.body: A clear reproduction, exact error text, selected game, template count, JSON name, and relevant screenshot are more useful than a general statement that it does not work.

pitfalls: Review reports before posting them publicly.
Do not include supporter keys, account credentials, or private save files.
Keep the generated job report when the problem happened during generation.

topics.title: Update KFPS and check its runtime
topics.summary: Use the built-in updater, keep personal folders in place, and understand what the Python checks mean.
steps: Open Update and choose Check Now.
Read the patch notes, then choose Update when a newer version is available.
Let KFPS close and run its existing updater. It reopens after a successful update.
If startup reports missing Python, confirm you downloaded the release that includes Python or installed the required runtime for the unbundled release.
Use Settings -> Open Logs when an update or runtime check fails.

sections.heading: What is preserved
sections.body: The updater is designed to preserve generated images, JSON outputs, editor projects, runtime data, local dependencies, and supporter-key data.

sections.heading: Release versus source
sections.body: GitHub's main/source ZIP is project code, not a supported app package. KFPS blocks that layout and points to the latest official release.

pitfalls: Do not unpack an update over a running KFPS process by hand.
Do not delete personal output folders to repair a missing runtime.
The release without bundled Python requires a working compatible Python installation and dependencies.

topics.title: Fix a broken or incomplete installation
topics.summary: Check that KFPS came from an official release and that its expected folders, executables, and runtime stayed together.
steps: Confirm the folder came from an official KFPS release, not GitHub's main/source ZIP.
Keep the full release folder together. Do not run only one copied EXE from another location.
For the bundled release, confirm its Python and dependency folders are still present.
Check antivirus quarantine if an executable or dependency disappeared.
Open Logs and keep the first missing-file or startup error.
Extract a fresh release to a new folder when the installation itself is damaged; move personal work only after the clean copy starts.

sections.heading: Two release types
sections.body: The bundled release includes Python and dependencies and is the simplest choice. The smaller unbundled release is for users who already maintain a compatible Python environment.

sections.heading: Personal files
sections.body: Generated jobs, images, editor projects, JSON outputs, reports, and key files are personal data. Back them up before replacing or cleaning an old installation.

pitfalls: Do not delete the whole folder before checking it for personal work.
Do not download random replacement DLL or Python files from third-party sites.
Do not report a source ZIP as a broken release; download the latest release first.

topics.title: Fix import or export
topics.summary: Check the game screen, group state, exact layer count, permissions, and whether the action is online or offline.
steps: Decide whether you are using online live-memory transfer or offline local-save transfer.
For online transfer, confirm the game is running and the vinyl group itself is open in Vinyl Group Editor.
For FH6 online import, reopen the saved circle template and ungroup it.
Enter the exact number of layers in the open game group or template.
Close the game before an offline write, then scan the correct game saves again.
Retry once after reopening the correct group. If access is denied, run KFPS with the same or higher permission level as the game.
Keep the transfer log and copy the first clear error if it still fails.

sections.heading: No safe group found
sections.body: KFPS could not verify a live layer table. The usual causes are the wrong editor screen, a grouped template, a wrong count, or a game process that restarted.

sections.heading: Null or stale layer
sections.body: The editor state changed after location or a different duplicate group matched part of the check. Reopen the intended group, remove duplicate templates above it, and retry without changing menus.

sections.heading: Offline save not found
sections.body: Make sure the selected game has created a local save for this Windows profile. Cloud-only, moved, locked, or actively open saves may not be available for offline editing.

pitfalls: Do not keep retrying live writes while changing menus in the game.
Do not offline-edit a save while the game is open.
Do not discard backup files until the game loads and saves the result correctly.

topics.title: Fix wrong, missing, or swapped shapes
topics.summary: Separate a bad JSON from a bad live preview, wrong game resources, stale template state, or an editor display issue.
steps: Open the JSON preview in Outputs or the manual editor. If it is already wrong there, the file or conversion is the problem.
If the KFPS preview is correct but the live game view is wrong, save the vinyl and reopen it once before judging.
Confirm the correct game target was selected because shape resource numbers differ between games.
For FH6, reopen and ungroup a clean template, enter its exact layer count, and import again.
Check that the JSON fits the template and that Clear Extra Template Layers is enabled.
Keep screenshots of both the KFPS preview and the reopened game result if the mismatch remains.

sections.heading: Centered blob
sections.body: When several groups collapse to one center, the export likely lost each group's accumulated position. Use the game-specific offline export path and report which source and game created the file.

sections.heading: Community shapes
sections.body: A low-resolution or incorrect community shape in the editor may be a renderer or resource-map issue, not damaged geometry. Compare it with the game or another known viewer before replacing shapes.

sections.heading: Live preview versus saved result
sections.body: Forza can show temporary resource or thumbnail state immediately after a write. Saving and reopening is the reliable comparison point.

pitfalls: Do not overwrite the last known-good saved group while diagnosing a mismatch.
Do not assume every game uses the same shape code for the same-looking asset.
Do not compare a raw checkpoint with a finalized preview as if they are identical files.

topics.title: Ask for help effectively
topics.summary: Send the smallest set of facts that lets someone reproduce or identify the problem without exposing private data.
steps: Copy Support Info from Help or create a local report from Settings.
State the KFPS version, Windows version, game, and whether the action was online or offline.
Write the exact buttons or steps used from a fresh app start.
Copy the first clear error and a few lines around it rather than only saying it crashed.
For generation, include the source type, preset, shape limit, last completed checkpoint, and job report.
For transfer, include the JSON name and shape count, exact template count, editor screen, and grouped or ungrouped state.
Add a screenshot that shows the full relevant window, then remove private names or paths before sharing.

sections.heading: Never share
sections.body: Do not send supporter keys, activation receipts, account credentials, private game saves, purchase files, or personal artwork unless you deliberately choose to.

sections.heading: A useful short report
sections.body: Example: KFPS version, Windows 11, FH6 online import, 3000-layer saved/reopened template ungrouped, selected 1842-shape final JSON, then the exact first error line.

pitfalls: A cropped screenshot that hides the selected game, count, or status may remove the useful clue.
Do not paste thousands of repeated progress lines when the first failure line is enough.
Review logs and reports for local filenames and Windows usernames before posting publicly.

topics.title: Know the current limits
topics.summary: KFPS is powerful, but game budgets, source quality, save formats, and live editor state still set hard boundaries.
steps: Keep each design within the target game's supported shape and layer budget.
Use a source with enough visible information; the generator cannot recover details that do not exist.
Keep backups of editor projects, generated jobs, JSONs, and game saves used for offline work.
Treat live-memory and save-file features as game-version-specific. Update KFPS after a game update.
Use final previews and a saved/reopened game result as the quality check.

sections.heading: Generation
sections.body: KFPS approximates pixels with a limited library of vector shapes. More search work and more layers can help, but exact photographic reproduction is not possible within a fixed game budget.

sections.heading: Transfer
sections.body: Online tools depend on the running game's current memory layout. Offline tools depend on supported local save formats. A game update can require a locator or format update before transfer works again.

sections.heading: Manual work
sections.body: Text, exact logos, tiny facial features, masks, and deliberate line work often benefit from the manual editor even after a strong generation.

pitfalls: Do not test risky offline changes without a restorable backup.
Do not assume a tool for one game or save version is safe for another.
Do not delete source images or projects after producing only one exported JSON.
